en.profile: Ahmed Azeez is a public health researcher and lecturer specialising in infectious disease epidemiology, surveillance, modelling, biostatistics, psychometric methods, and instrument development.
en.education: Ahmed completed a PhD in Community Medicine and Public Health at Universiti Sains Malaysia from 2021 to 2025, specialising in infectious disease epidemiology. He completed a Master’s Degree in Community Health at Middle Technical University in Baghdad from 2015 to 2018 and a Bachelor’s Degree in Community Health at the same university from 2006 to 2010.
en.positions: Ahmed is a Lecturer at the Higher Health Institute of Wasit, Iraq, where he teaches emergency health, public health, and epidemiology, supervises student research, mentors students, and contributes to curriculum development. Earlier, he worked as a Community Health Specialist in the Maternal and Child Health Division of Wasit’s Public Health Department from 2018 to 2021, and as a Public Health Officer from 2010 to 2015.
en.research: His research interests include infectious disease epidemiology and modelling, community-based disease surveillance, community engagement and participation, public health programme evaluation, epidemiological study design, questionnaire adaptation and validation, and quantitative and psychometric methods in public health.
en.methods: His methods and software include exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, Item Response Theory, structural equation modelling, path analysis, epidemiological study design, R, Mplus, JAMOVI, JASP, and SPSS. He is a WHO-certified e-instructor and holds a Training of Trainers qualification for health-worker training.
en.publications: Selected scholarly outputs examine community engagement and participation in community-based infectious disease surveillance, knowledge-attitudes-perceptions questionnaire development and validation, and structural equation modelling of social and behavioural factors. They include articles in the Journal of Public Health Research, Osong Public Health and Research Perspectives, the International Journal of One Health, and the Medical Journal of Babylon, plus a published book chapter. The About page contains the detailed publication list.
en.conferences: Ahmed presented research at the 14th IMT-GT UNINET Bioscience Conference 2025, the 1st Kedah International Health Conference 2025, the 4th International Conference on Medical and Health Sciences and related symposium, and the Social Science Postgraduate International Seminar at Universiti Sains Malaysia.
en.ongoing: Current research includes Bayesian hierarchical and negative binomial regression analysis of the spatiotemporal dynamics of four zoonotic public health threats in Wasit Governorate, Iraq, from 2022 to 2025, and cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of an Arabic Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices questionnaire for breast cancer screening.
posts: Key Epidemiological Indicators for Public Health Data Analysis explains incidence, prevalence, mortality rate, case fatality rate, attack rate, and relative risk.
ROC Curves and AUC: Useful Measures, Not the Whole Story explains discrimination, sensitivity, specificity, calibration, fairness, causality, and public-health use.
Python for Public Health Epidemiology discusses Python as a practical open-source option alongside R for surveillance analysis, visualization, modelling, and reproducible notebooks.
How to Handle Outliers in Data Analysis discusses checking whether an outlier is real, detecting it, capping it, transforming a variable, analysing it separately, or retaining it with an explanation.
Machine Learning Algorithms introduces supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, and reinforcement learning.
Five Common Relationships Among Three Variables in Statistics explains covariates, confounding, mediation, and moderation in relation to X, Y, and Z.
